identityReview: Maia Sandu, born May 24, 1972 in Risipeni, Moldova. Management graduate, international-relations master and Harvard MC/MPA 2010, not MPP or PhD. World Bank executive-director adviser, not executive director. Education minister July 2012–July 2015; PAS founder/chair from 2016, resigned chair December 2020. Prime minister June–November 2019 with no-confidence November 12 and successor sworn November 14. Moldova’s first female president from December 24, 2020, second term from December 24, 2024 after November 3 runoff victory. Current president, not prime minister or current PAS chair. Moldova remains an EU candidate in negotiations.
lifeStatusEvidence: MOLDPRES reports a completed Brussels meeting with European Council President António Costa and Sandu’s participation/remarks at the enlargement forum. Indexed original publication November 16, 2026 at 19:05 and the separately read official Costa weekly schedule support November 16. The page’s current-date header and relative age are not substituted for the event date. November 17 Reuters drone-statement report was search-indexed but the full article was inaccessible and is not claimed as fully reviewed direct evidence.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read official presidential biography, Harvard Gazette degree account, MOLDPRES party-registration record, Xinhua cabinet-dismissal and successor-oath reports, EU accession pages, Constitutional Court validation excerpts, Interfax actual-inauguration account, official ODIHR final-findings summary and MOLDPRES completed-meeting report. Read official Costa schedule for corroboration, and Commons portrait/parent metadata with photographer credit and licence-review record. No portrait pixels.
corrections: Read the official presidential biography for birthday May 24, 1972 in Risipeni, 1994 management graduation, 1995–1998 international-relations studies, 2010–2012 World Bank adviser role, education ministry July 2012–July 2015, party founding and resignation, 2019 premiership and both December 24 presidential accessions. Its Harvard public-policy degree wording conflicts with Harvard’s own MC/MPA record; use Harvard. Adviser to an executive director is not the executive director or World Bank president. No assumption that party founder remains party chair.

Read Harvard Gazette’s March 29, 2022 announcement, including degree designation and prior studies/career. The awarded degree is the Mid-Career Master in Public Administration, MC/MPA 2010, not MPP. Mid-career describes the program, not proof she studied part-time while employed. The announcement’s shorthand about a December election is superseded by the presidential record’s November 15 vote and December 24 inauguration. A scheduled graduation speech is not proof it occurred; promotional praise is not independent measurement of corruption reduction.

Read MOLDPRES’s May 26, 2016 registration report. Distinguish the December 23, 2015 political-movement announcement, May 15 founding congress, May 19 submission and May 26 Justice Ministry registration. Contemporary party membership counts and then-current appointments are not carried into 2026 as current. The original article date is separate from the site’s moving current-date header.

Read Xinhua’s November 12, 2019 no-confidence account: 63 of 101 deputies supported dismissal, and the cabinet had taken office June 8. The dispute concerned Sandu’s proposed role in preselecting prosecutor-general candidates, not a criminal conviction of her or a sole unilateral final appointment. ACUM–Socialist coalition and head-of-government status are distinct from the presidency held by Dodon.

Read Xinhua’s completed successor-government swearing-in account. Dateline/event November 14, 2019 differs from November 15 page timestamp; Chicu’s cabinet received confidence and took the oath on November 14 after Sandu’s November 12 no-confidence vote. The article’s forecasts about government lifespan and reform promises are not adopted as fulfilled outcomes.

Read the European Commission country page’s current candidate-country label and relevant accession chronology/search-indexed material. The latest-news entries concern an ongoing process, not completed membership. No exhaustive chapter-by-chapter or full 2026 Commission country-report audit claimed.

Read the Council/European Council policy page’s accession sections. March 3, 2022 application, June 23 candidate decision, December 2023 political opening decision, June 21, 2024 negotiating framework and June 25 conference are distinct. The page also records October 13, 2026 opening of clusters 2 and 3. Public text acknowledges ongoing progress without claiming all negotiations closed, a fixed accession date or sole personal responsibility.

Read the first accession-conference page. It identifies the June 25, 2024 meeting and Moldova’s delegation led by Prime Minister Dorin Recean. Sandu’s policy advocacy is not a personal signature of an accession treaty or personal chairing of that delegation. Candidate and member status remain distinct.

Read selected substantive sections of the Constitutional Court’s 2024 election-validation account: two rounds October 20 and November 3, CEC November 9 result, 930,139 votes for Sandu versus 750,430 for Stoianoglo, and validation requirements. The court confirmed the result while discussing vote-buying and electoral problems; validation is not a claim that no irregularity existed. Court records non-party status before validation, distinct from PAS support. No full underlying case file or individual vote-buying prosecution reviewed.

Read Interfax’s December 24, 2024 completed swearing-in report and final 55.35% runoff result. It independently corroborates the official biography’s second-term inauguration and 2020 victory over Dodon. The November 3 runoff is not October 20’s first round; no direct quotation of the oath or ceremonial speech reproduced. This historic event is not evidence of current personal activity.

Read ODIHR’s official March 24, 2025 summary of final findings and recommendations on the 2024 presidential election and referendum. Preserve both positive administration/free-campaign findings and unequal-opportunity criticism involving favourable incumbent coverage and overlapping campaigns. This is a summary page, not a claimed full final-report PDF review. Do not convert observation findings into a criminal conviction or annulment of the election.

Read MOLDPRES’s substantive completed Brussels meeting and enlargement-forum report, quoting Costa after meeting Sandu and describing her remarks. Search metadata dates publication November 16 at 19:05; the rendered global date header moves to November 18 and relative-age text varies. The official Costa schedule independently places the meeting on November 16, but the schedule alone is not proof of attendance. Combined with the retrospective report it supports the date. Early-2028 negotiation closure is Sandu’s goal, not completed membership; anticipated opening of remaining clusters is not recorded as already done.
